STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plate: a typical square dinner plate is 20-30 cm; this one looks large-ish, so I estimate about 26 cm across.
b) Reference: the plate's edge is roughly 3 fork-lengths at the visible width (fork ~19 cm, so the fork-equivalent check suggests ~25-27 cm). Trusting both cues: width ≈ 26 cm, area ≈ 676 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Steak slices (2 pieces of beef, about 9 x 5 cm, plus a smaller piece under it): footprint ≈ 60 cm², thickness ~1.5 cm average → 90 ml x 1.0 = ~90 g. Include the smaller top slice: total ~110 g.
- Mashed potato (mound, ~10 x 8 cm footprint ≈ 65 cm², average ~2 cm) → 130 ml x 1.0 = ~130 g.
- Cheese-topped item (gratin/flatbread-type piece, ~10 x 7 cm ≈ 55 cm², ~1.5 cm thick) → 80 ml x 1.0 = ~80 g.
- Zucchini and roasted vegetables (pieces spread across ~60 cm², ~1.2 cm average) → 70 ml x 0.6 = ~45 g.
- Wilted greens under the steak (small, ~15 cm², ~0.5 cm) → 7 ml x 0.6 ≈ 5 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the greens sit under the meat, already counted. No significant hidden base layer; total ≈ 430 g.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served, cooked):
- Beef steak: ~200 kcal/100 g (110 g → 220 kcal)
- Mashed potato: ~110 kcal/100 g (130 g → 143 kcal)
- Cheese-topped piece: ~250 kcal/100 g (80 g → 200 kcal)
- Roasted zucchini/vegetables: ~80 kcal/100 g (45 g → 36 kcal, oil included roughly)
- Cooked greens: ~25 kcal/100 g (5 g → 1 kcal)

Total ≈ 430 g, ≈ 600 kcal.
